title: Finite substructures: ages and amalgamation

based_on.title: Model Theory Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 58–61 (§6.1, Proposition 6.1 and the necessity of amalgamation in Theorem 6.6)

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Determine which collections of finite relational structures occur inside one countable structure, and why finite symmetries require amalgamation.
abstract: Which finite patterns can occur inside one countable structure? In a language with finitely many relations, its finite induced substructures form its age. This collection is closed under taking smaller pieces, and any two pieces occur together in a larger one. Conversely, these two conditions suffice to construct a countable structure with exactly the prescribed finite pieces. Joining pieces becomes more demanding when they already share a specified part: amalgamation requires the two placements of that part to agree. We prove that amalgamation is necessary whenever every isomorphism between finite pieces extends to a symmetry of the whole structure, and work out finite sets as an example.
